The two edges leaving C and their targets, B and D, are in the accent color; A and E point into C and are not successors. The card lists B, D." width="100%"} Returns the nodes that the specified node points *to*, i.e., every `v` for which an edge `node -> v` exists. This is a thin wrapper around `neighbors(node, mode="out")` that refuses to run on undirected graphs, where "outgoing" has no meaning. Successors answer "where can I go from here in one step?", which is useful for: - listing the tasks that become unblocked once a task finishes - finding the pages a page links to, or the accounts a user follows - stepping forward through a DAG or state machine (see `trav_out()` for doing this on a selection) Only one hop is examined; use `select_nodes_in_neighborhood(mode="out")` for multi-hop downstream sets. The result is a list of node IDs (not labels) and the selection is not changed. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node whose successors are wanted, given as an integer node ID or a string label. An unknown label raises `ValueError`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node IDs of all targets of edges leaving `node=`. Empty if the node has no outgoing edges. Each successor appears once even if there are parallel edges to it (as in `get_predecessors()`), in the order of its first edge. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected, or if `node=` is an ID or label not found in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Likewise, `get_successors()` wraps `neighbors(mode="out")` -- here "A" points to both "B" and "C", while the edge from "D" into "A" is ignored: ::: {#bbab50f5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) graph.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("D", "A")]) successors = graph.get_successors("A") [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in successors] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['B', 'C'] ``` ::: ::: Successors and predecessors are mirror images: every successor of "A" has "A" among its predecessors. Checking this for "B" confirms the edge direction: ::: {#bf868e6a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} b_preds = graph.get_predecessors("B") [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in b_preds] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['A'] ``` ::: :::
